candidates.name: Kitchen Witch (Practical Magic 2-era witchy apothecary kitchen)
candidates.summary: A cozy, old-world witchy kitchen look - labeled herb and apothecary jars, dried flowers, candles, copper, moons - that Pinterest named a fall-2026 trend and that Practical Magic 2 pushed into the mainstream.
candidates.what: Kitchen Witch is a decor and hobby aesthetic built on herbs and home craft: apothecary-style labeled jars on open shelves, drying herbs and flowers, homemade spice blends, beeswax candles and vintage 'old-world' decor. It sits between cottagecore and the 90s whimsigoth look made famous by the 1998 film Practical Magic. In 2026 Pinterest gave it a name, and the September 2026 sequel brought licensed retail collections.

origin.text: Long-standing witchy/cottage-witch subculture and 1998 Practical Magic nostalgia. Pinterest named 'Kitchen Witch' in its 2026 Hobbies Trend Report (released around 2026-08-25, data May 2025 vs May 2026), shortly before Practical Magic 2 opened at No. 1 on the weekend of Sept 11-13, 2026.

adopters.text: Pinterest hobby users pursuing herbal crafts (herbal apothecary, spice blends, candle making); TikTok creators doing Practical Magic-inspired kitchen makeovers, including renters; nostalgic millennial fans of the 1998 film; whimsigoth and dark-cottage decor fans. Why they care: hands-on, offline hobbies plus a nostalgic, cozy seasonal look.

spread.text: The trend shows up independently in Pinterest's own data, consumer press, real-estate/design press (Inman), TikTok creator clusters, and retail licensing (Target, Wayfair, MacKenzie-Childs). Much of the press restates Pinterest's numbers, so those articles are one signal. The film is a strong, separate catalyst.

trajectory.text: Accelerating into October: Pinterest reports large increases (May-to-May), and the film's No. 1 opening plus licensed collections pushed the look into mass retail in September. Expect the film spike to fade after Halloween. The underlying witchy/herbal hobby is long-lived, so a smaller winter (Yule/solstice) tail is plausible (inference). No time-series data (Google Trends) could be measured.

productDemand.text: Purchase-adjacent signals: big retailers licensed decor and apparel (Wayfair, MacKenzie-Childs, Target), and fan goods sell on Etsy at $8 (digital prints) to $44 (sweaters). The Pinterest searches are utility/hobby intent ('herbal apothecary', 'homemade spice blends', 'candle making tutorial'), which fits functional printables like jar labels and recipe/herb journals. No sales figures were seen.

competition.text: Halloween-style potion/apothecary labels (Eye of Newt and similar) are already sold as downloads on Payhip and Etsy, and Practical Magic-inspired signs, pins, sweaters and prints exist. Licensed brands now hold the film-branded space. Counts could not be measured. The visible supply leans toward Halloween novelty and film references, not functional year-round herb/pantry systems.

gap.text: An original, non-film, non-Halloween 'kitchen witch pantry' system: functional labels for real culinary herbs, spices, teas and homemade blends (plus editable blanks) in a vintage-apothecary look, paired with a herb/recipe 'grimoire' journal. This serves the utility searches (herbal apothecary, spice blends) and stays sellable after Oct 31 and as Yule/holiday gifts.

window.estimate: Now through about late December 2026 for digital products; POD only for holiday/Yule gifting, not Halloween.
window.reasoning: Digital delivery is instant, but new listings take weeks to be discovered, so Halloween demand (27 days away) is mostly out of reach. The aesthetic is autumn-winter rather than Halloween-only: herbs, candles and cozy kitchens carry into winter solstice/Yule (Dec 21) and holiday gifting. The film's home release could create a second spike, but its date was not verified.
invalidators: Interest collapses right after Halloween (watch Pinterest/Etsy engagement on test pins and listings in early November)
Licensed Practical Magic 2 goods and Halloween label sellers crowd out new listings
IP complaints if listings use the film's name, characters or lines
window.seasonality: Peaks Sept-Oct (Halloween + film); secondary tail around winter solstice/Yule and holiday gifting; herb-pantry labels are useful year-round.

rights.note: Do NOT use 'Practical Magic', Owens-family names, film stills, logos, or film lines such as 'midnight margaritas' in designs, titles or tags. Warner Bros. is actively licensing (Target, Wayfair, MacKenzie-Childs), so enforcement is likely. Generic 'kitchen witch', apothecary, herb and moon motifs are fine. Treat witchcraft respectfully: frame herb content as culinary or traditional folklore, never as promised effects.

timing.rationale: Strong, current catalyst (Sept 2026 film + Aug 2026 Pinterest report), but Halloween is too close for new-listing discovery; digital products can still catch the autumn-to-Yule tail.

buyerIntent.rationale: Licensed retail collections and existing fan goods at $8-$44 suggest people buy into the look; Pinterest searches show utility intent (herbal apothecary, spice blends). No sales data.

supplyGap.rationale: Halloween potion labels and film-inspired goods already exist; the gap is narrower: functional, non-IP, year-round herb/pantry systems.

productFit.rationale: Labels, journals and herb charts are quick to design with common tools and AI-assisted ornament; no inventory.

durability.rationale: The film spike will fade, but witchy/cottage-witch decor and herbal hobbies have persisted for years (Practical Magic 1998 cult status, whimsigoth).

economics.rationale: Digital downloads carry near-zero marginal cost at typical low price points; KDP/POD prints have thinner margins. No revenue forecast implied.

candidates.actionRationale: Evidence of demand comes from several independent sources: Pinterest-reported utility searches, a No. 1 film, and broad retail licensing. There is a credible original product angle (functional herb-pantry labels and a herb/recipe journal) that avoids the film's IP. Digital products can launch within days and still catch the autumn-to-Yule window. Test with digital only. Skip Halloween-specific designs and POD for Halloween.

products.buyer: Home cooks and herbal hobbyists (mostly US women 25-45) restyling open shelves or a spice cabinet in the witchy-cottage look
products.theme: 'Kitchen Witch Pantry' apothecary label system: 60+ labels for real culinary herbs, spices, teas and homemade blends (rosemary, sage, chamomile, lavender, cinnamon, 'Hearth Blend'...), vintage-apothecary typography with moon and botanical ornament, plus editable blanks (Canva link + PDF) and round/rectangular sizes for mason and spice jars
products.whyBuy: Matches the Pinterest utility searches ('herbal apothecary', homemade spice blends) and the labeled-jar look central to TikTok kitchen makeovers; still useful after Halloween.
products.differentiation: Functional and year-round (real ingredients, editable), not Halloween novelty labels like 'Eye of Newt'; no film references.
products.validationTest: Publish one Etsy listing and one Gumroad page, plus 10 Pinterest pins (styled shelf mockups) that link to them; run for 21 days.
products.continueIf: Pins earn saves/outbound clicks above your account baseline and the listing gets favorites plus at least a few sales within 21 days.
products.pivotIf: Pins get saves but no sales: try a free 12-label sampler as a lead magnet or bundle with the journal; or reposition as 'apothecary spice labels' without the witch framing.
products.stopIf: Almost no impressions or saves after 21 days and 20+ pins, or clicks without conversions after two price/thumbnail changes.
products.rightsNote: Original typography and ornament only; avoid film names, quotes and imagery; use public-domain or self-made botanical art.

products.buyer: Gift buyers for witchy, cottagecore or herb-loving friends (Yule/solstice and holiday gifts), and the hobbyists themselves
products.theme: 'Kitchen Grimoire' herb and recipe journal: herb profile pages (culinary use, harvest, storage), blend recipe cards, a seasonal 'wheel of the year' kitchen calendar, and pressed-flower pages; sold as a printable PDF and as an Amazon KDP paperback
products.whyBuy: Ties to Pinterest-reported spice-blend, candle and herbal-apothecary hobby searches; journal format suits holiday gifting.
products.differentiation: Practical recipe/herb log with an old-world look rather than a spell book; no film IP; content framed as culinary and traditional folklore.
products.validationTest: Sell the printable PDF on Etsy first (instant) for two weeks; publish the KDP paperback in parallel by about mid-October so it is live for holiday shopping.
products.continueIf: The PDF converts at least as well as the label set, or KDP shows organic sales by mid-November.
products.pivotIf: Buyers prefer the labels: fold journal pages into a larger 'Kitchen Witch Pantry' bundle.
products.stopIf: No sales from either format by early December.
products.rightsNote: Write original herb notes; do not present herbs as remedies or promise effects; no film references.

products.buyer: Renters and homeowners styling a kitchen or coffee nook in the whimsigoth/kitchen-witch look
products.theme: Vintage herbarium-style culinary herb chart and moon-phase apothecary prints (set of 3) in deep jewel tones, sold as digital downloads with an optional POD print
products.whyBuy: Design press recommends botanicals and apothecary-flair decor for the fall 2026 whimsigoth look; renters can decorate without remodeling.
products.differentiation: Functional chart content (culinary pairings, harvest months) instead of a film-quote sign; consistent with the label set for cross-selling.
products.validationTest: Add as a digital listing and as a bundle add-on to the label set; track attach rate.
products.continueIf: The bundle with prints sells as well as or better than labels alone.
products.pivotIf: Prints don't attach: offer them free as Pinterest-traffic bait.
products.stopIf: Zero standalone sales and no bundle lift after 3 weeks.
products.rightsNote: Use public-domain botanical illustrations (verify pre-1931 publication) or original art; no film imagery.

unresolved: When Practical Magic 2 reaches home viewing (digital/streaming) - not verified, and it could create a second spike.
Actual Etsy listing counts and sales velocity for 'kitchen witch labels' / 'apothecary spice labels' (Etsy not accessible).
Whether Pinterest's global May-to-May increases reflect US buyers specifically, and how much of the interest ends at Halloween.
Pinterest figures were seen only through search summaries of the newsroom page, not the page itself.

candidates.name: Cosmic Reset (beginner astrology, tarot and astrocartography)
candidates.summary: A fall-2026 wave of people learning astrology and tarot from scratch - natal charts, astrocartography, moon rituals - which Pinterest reports among its biggest search increases.
candidates.what: Pinterest's 'Cosmic Reset' trend covers beginners learning astrology basics, pulling natal charts, exploring astrocartography (mapping places onto a birth chart), learning tarot and crystal meanings, and doing moon or 'reset' rituals around September's fresh start. It rides on long-standing Gen Z/millennial interest in astrology, but the reported growth is concentrated in 'for beginners' and 'learn' queries.

origin.text: Long-running astrology/tarot interest among Gen Z and millennials. Pinterest named the 'Cosmic Reset' trend in its 2026 Hobbies Trend Report (around 2026-08-25; May 2025 vs May 2026 searches).

adopters.text: Beginners (largely Gen Z and millennial women, inferred from coverage) who want to learn the system themselves rather than read horoscopes; travelers using astrocartography; people building September/New-Year 'reset' routines. Why they care: self-reflection, identity language, and intentional routines.

spread.text: Beyond Pinterest's own data, astrocartography shows up in travel press (Frommer's, BreezyScroll), and astrology is used as a shopping frame in mainstream gift editorial (E! Online). Pinterest Predicts separately reported a celestial/opalescent decor appetite. The Hobbies-report press coverage (WWD, VITA, Social Media Today) restates one data source.

trajectory.text: Astrology/tarot is a long-established niche (commentary from 2025 already describes rising Gen Z interest). Pinterest's 2026 report suggests a renewed beginner-led wave, with the largest percentage increases in the report. Without time-series data it is unclear whether this is accelerating or a September seasonal bump; New-Year intention-setting usually brings another lift (inference).

productDemand.text: The reported searches are learning/curiosity intent ('learn astrology', 'tarot cards for beginners', 'crystals and meanings'), which suits workbooks, journals and planners better than decor. Astrology already works as a gift frame in mainstream editorial. No sales evidence for astrology printables was gathered.

competition.text: Not measured: the search budget ran out before a marketplace check. From background knowledge (unverified this session), astrology/moon planners and tarot journals have been sold on Etsy and KDP for years, so competition is probably high; a beginner 'learn the system' workbook may be less crowded.

gap.text: A 'learning-first' product that matches the beginner queries: a structured 12-week workbook that teaches how to read your own chart (fill-in chart wheel, glossary, guided worksheets) without predictions, plus an astronomically accurate 2027 moon-phase reflection planner timed for New Year.

window.estimate: Launch by early-to-mid December 2026 for New-Year buying; the beginner workbook can sell longer.
window.reasoning: Planner and intention products sell mostly from late November through January. A new listing needs weeks to gain visibility, so prepare now and list by early December. Digital delivery suits last-minute buyers.
invalidators: Marketplace check shows saturated beginner-astrology workbooks with strong incumbents
Pinterest beginner-astrology interest proves to be a September-only bump
window.seasonality: September 'reset' and January New-Year intention peaks.

rights.note: Belief-based: describe astrology and tarot as reflective practices, explain the community's methods accurately, never promise outcomes or predictions. Tarot art: draw original cards or verify that any reference art is in the public domain (the 1909 Rider-Waite-Smith originals are commonly treated as US public domain, but later recolored editions are claimed by their publishers). Moon-phase and eclipse dates must come from an authoritative astronomical source and be checked.

candidates.name: Poetcore (the poet aesthetic)
candidates.summary: A literary, romantic style - tweed and turtlenecks, satchels, notebooks and dog-eared poetry books - that Pinterest predicted for 2026 and fashion press now calls an autumn-2026 trend.
candidates.what: Poetcore dresses like a 19th-century or bohemian poet: oversized turtlenecks, vintage blazers, messenger satchels, scarves, ink-stained notebooks and books carried as accessories. It is a softer, more romantic relative of dark academia and is marketed to both women and men. Its props (notebooks, poetry, handwriting) map naturally onto stationery and literary wall art.

origin.text: Grew out of dark/light academia and literary TikTok/Pinterest culture. Pinterest named it in Pinterest Predicts 2026 (released about Dec 9, 2025 per press dates; data Sept 2024-Aug 2025).

adopters.text: Gen Z and young millennial fashion followers of both genders; book lovers; fans of literary-heartthrob celebrity style (inferred). They care because it signals introspection, slowness and taste rather than logos.

spread.text: Has moved from Pinterest's prediction into international fashion press (FashionUnited editions, Soigne Middle East, nss g-club, LDN Fashion) and retailer merchandising blogs (US boutique, Tokyo Canvas). The FashionUnited regional editions are one syndicated signal.

trajectory.text: Coverage runs from the Dec 2025 prediction through spring 2026 merchandising to 'autumn 2026's most literary trend', which points to sustained growth in fashion. No 2026 search time-series or decor/stationery demand data was found, so the spread into paper goods is unproven.

productDemand.text: Commercial uptake is visible in apparel merchandising only. Demand for Poetcore stationery, journals or poetry prints is plausible (books and notebooks are core props) but not evidenced. Gifting for book lovers in Q4 is a reasonable channel (inference).

competition.text: Not measured (search budget exhausted). Literary/dark-academia prints and journals are a long-established category (background knowledge, unverified), so generic designs would face competition.

gap.text: Curated public-domain poetry broadsides typeset in letterpress style, plus a 'commonplace book' journal for copying and annotating lines, sold as a Poetcore set. This uses rights-free text and fits gifting, New-Year journaling, Valentine's and National Poetry Month (April).

window.estimate: Autumn 2026 through spring 2027 (aesthetic likely outlasts the season).
window.reasoning: Multi-source fashion adoption plus runway support suggests more than a single-season micro-trend; the paper-goods market is not time-critical, so creators can test without racing Halloween.
invalidators: Poetcore fashion coverage drops off after autumn 2026
Marketplace check shows literary prints/journals are saturated with no premium for the Poetcore framing
window.seasonality: Autumn/winter look; poetry gifting peaks for Valentine's and April (National Poetry Month).

rights.note: Use only poems in the US public domain (published before 1931, e.g., Dickinson, Keats, Christina Rossetti, Whitman) and check each text and edition. Avoid modern poets and song lyrics. Don't use celebrity likenesses associated with the look.

timing.rationale: Fashion momentum is real, but no evidence yet that it drives paper-goods buying this quarter; not time-critical.

buyerIntent.rationale: Searches and press are style/curiosity; apparel merchandising exists; no stationery purchase evidence.

supplyGap.rationale: Competition not measured; literary prints are assumed to be an established category, with a gap only for curated Poetcore-framed sets.

productFit.rationale: Typesetting public-domain poems and building KDP journals is fast and cheap.

durability.rationale: Spread across many outlets and regions and adjacent to long-lived dark academia; runway support reported.

economics.rationale: Digital prints and KDP journals have workable margins at low price points; POD posters thinner.

candidates.actionRationale: The aesthetic is durable and suits paper goods, but there is no evidence of product demand and competition was not checked. Watch for Poetcore-specific stationery or print demand (Pinterest/Etsy signals). Optionally build a small public-domain poetry print set now at low cost for Valentine's and April tests.

products.buyer: Book lovers and Poetcore/dark-academia fans decorating reading nooks or dorms; gift buyers
products.theme: Letterpress-style broadsides of public-domain poems (set of 4-6: Dickinson, Keats, Christina Rossetti, Whitman) on aged paper with ink-blot ornament
products.whyBuy: Poems and books are core props of the look; a rights-free, giftable decor piece.
products.differentiation: Curated, accurately transcribed texts with typographic craft instead of generic quote posters.
products.validationTest: List the set as a digital download plus 10 pins tagged poetcore/literary decor; compare saves against your other boards.
products.continueIf: Saves and favorites are steady and a few sales come within 4 weeks.
products.pivotIf: Saves but no sales: make one poem free as a pin magnet and sell the journal instead.
products.stopIf: No traction after 4 weeks and 20 pins.
products.rightsNote: Verify public-domain status and text accuracy for each poem.

products.buyer: Poetcore adopters who journal; New-Year journaling buyers
products.theme: 'Commonplace Book' journal: pages for copying lines, annotating poems, word lists and drafting, with a monthly 'poem to memorize' page (public-domain selections); KDP paperback + printable
products.whyBuy: Notebooks are part of the look; commonplace books suit the slow, literary values the trend is described with.
products.differentiation: Built for engaging with poetry, not a blank notebook.
products.validationTest: Publish on KDP and as a PDF in December; promote around New Year.
products.pivotIf: Re-theme for Valentine's (love poems) if January is flat.
products.stopIf: No sales by end of February.

Competition levels for literary prints and journals (not measured).
